item.title: Newton Fair and Affordable Housing Partnership Recommends Further Support for Housing Initiatives
item.description: Newton’s Fair and Affordable Housing Partnership met on Tuesday, urging the city to prioritize studying and strengthening its existing affordable housing programs before pursuing major policy initiatives, specifically highlighting the importance of building community support within affordable housing initiatives.

item.title: BC Breaks Eight-Game Losing Streak With Last-Second 68–67 Win Over Wake Forest
item.description: Aidan Shaw played the hero for Boston College men's basketball on Wednesday night, hitting a last-second tip-in to give the Eagles a 68–67 win over Wake Forest to break their eight-game losing streak.

item.title: Author Yiyun Li Discusses Time, Idiosyncrasy, and the Writing Process
item.description: On Wednesday night, students, professors, and Boston locals flooded into Gasson to hear Yiyun Li, author of 12 books and a multitude of short stories, memoirs, and essays, speak as part of the Lowell Humanities Series, presented by Boston College’s English department.

item.title: Innovation in Action: One Student’s Push to Improve Memory Care
item.description: After spending years volunteering in hospitals and nursing homes, Jonathan Xue witnessed patients’ gradual memory deterioration, and developed accessible, at-home cognitive tests.

item.title: Spring Break Film Watchlist
item.description: I believe that films centered around young adulthood, travel, and young-adult stories are fitting for spring vacation. With this in mind, here is a list of five films that fit the overall sentiment of Spring Break.

item.title: From Punta To Passing Time on the Couch: A Spring Break Playlist
item.description: This playlist is a way of splitting the difference between a plethora of vibes and reawakening your appreciation for life, no matter where you’re spending your Spring Break.

item.title: Newton Police Investigate Mystery Pig Leg Near Auburndale Trail
item.description: The Newton Police Department (NPD) is investigating what they believe to be a full “pig leg or flank” found just off a walking trail near Flowed Meadow at the Auburndale Cove on Sunday.

item.title: Proposed Crafts Street Development Continues To Face Pushback From Zoning Board and Residents
item.description: The Newton Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA) met on Wednesday to hold its third hearing on a proposal for a 234-unit residential development on a 2.7-acre lot on Crafts Street in Nonantum. The applicant, Wood Partners, presented the updated model design, which was rejected at its last hearing, in hopes of acquiring a comprehensive permit...
